context: Tests whether the agent correctly distinguishes member-from-extension primitives in the Koog strategy DSL when emitting the import block. The natural tool-handling loop uses both shapes — `forwardTo` (member, no import), `onToolCalls` / `onTextMessage` (extensions in `ai.koog.agents.core.dsl.extension.*`, need explicit imports). Agents that copy-paste the call shape without resolving the import side typically over-import members or under-import extensions, which is the exact compile error this rubric grades against.

checklist.name: Imports the `onToolCalls` extension explicitly
checklist.description: The produced file contains a line like `import ai.koog.agents.core.dsl.extension.onToolCalls` (either fully-qualified named or as part of a star-import covering the same package). Without this import the `onToolCalls { ... }` edge call does not resolve

checklist.name: Imports the `onTextMessage` extension explicitly
checklist.description: Same as above for `onTextMessage` — `import ai.koog.agents.core.dsl.extension.onTextMessage` (or a star-import covering the package). The text-reply branch of the loop calls this extension

checklist.name: Does not invent a member import for `forwardTo`
checklist.description: The import block does NOT contain a line like `import ai.koog.agents.core.dsl.builder.forwardTo` (or any other variant of a top-level `forwardTo` import). `forwardTo` is an infix member on `AIAgentNodeBase`; inventing a top-level import for it produces an unresolved-reference error at compile

checklist.name: Uses both edge primitives the loop needs
checklist.description: The strategy body contains an `edge(... forwardTo nodeExecuteTool onToolCalls { ... })`-shape edge AND an `edge(... forwardTo nodeFinish onTextMessage { ... })`-shape edge (variable names may differ). Both branches are present — the agent didn't shortcut the loop into a single linear chain

checklist.name: Chains `nodeExecuteTools` to `nodeLLMSendToolResults` explicitly
checklist.description: After `nodeExecuteTools()` produces `ReceivedToolResults`, there is an edge feeding those into `nodeLLMSendToolResults()`. The 1.0 surface dropped the auto-writeback variant — without this edge the LLM never sees what its tools returned

checklist.name: Wires the loop back through `nodeExecuteTool` on continued tool calls
checklist.description: There is a back-edge from `nodeLLMSendToolResults` to `nodeExecuteTools` gated by `onToolCalls { ... }`, so a multi-step tool sequence loops rather than dying after the first tool result
